LanguageData.CC_Fealty_Topic: Swearing fealty to them ({WORD}; {RITE} by their ways), about {TRIBUTE} silver's worth each season
LanguageData.CC_SetNote_DiplomacyFealty: The colony may swear fealty to a stronger neighbor, and keep vassals of its own.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DiplomacyFealty_Tip: The colony may swear fealty to a people at peace with goodwill 40 or more and two towns or more within reach (never the Empire, whose titles and permits are its own), by a letter to their head, or when they offer their protection to a colony raided twice in a season with five fighters or fewer. Agreed, their head (or one who speaks for them) comes to the gate, anyone who objects (one sworn to vengeance on them, the proud, a devout colonist of another faith) has their say before the council, and the colony's speaker swears by their rite. Each season their collector comes to the gate for the tribute, 150 to 600 silver's worth by the colony's wealth; short, the rest is owed, and still owed at the next season's day the oath breaks (20 goodwill). When their town within reach is attacked they call the colony's levies, two fighters by caravan within five days (refused, 10 goodwill). When a home is raided their band comes without a call, at most once a season, nine times in ten; a season in which they failed lets the colony leave without blame. Renouncing is the council's question and costs their grudge, 30 goodwill. Vassals of the colony's own: the hamlet once sworn, and up to two struggling towns (under 20 prosperity for 30 days, at war elsewhere) that ask for its protection, at most one ask a year. At harvest their carter brings produce, light, usual or heavy as the council sets it (heavy costs 3 goodwill each season); the quartermaster collects a season's dues; the council may call their levies when a home is raided (a third of the threat, once a season), and their dead weigh on their head's regard; they ask for help, for the colony's judgement in a quarrel, or for a camp near them to be broken; a head sour for a season asks to be released, and refused they break away. Faction Territories' vassals get a head who writes and asks; their tribute, purchases and points stay that mod's. Off: nothing new is sworn or asked, and the oaths standing run on.

LanguageData.CC_Fealty_Risks: Tribute bites in a lean season: short, it is owed, and still owed at the next season's day the oath breaks ({BROKEN} goodwill). The levies fight in someone else's war and may be hurt or killed there; refused, {REFUSED} goodwill. Their enemies stay their own business. Renouncing the oath later costs their grudge ({RENOUNCE} goodwill), unless they failed to protect the colony.

LanguageData.CC_Vassal_Ask_Help: {WHO} writes from {TOWN}: the season has gone hard there, and they ask the colony for {OTHER}.

LanguageData.CC_Vassal_AskWhat_Judgement: Side with {TOWN}, and its head thinks better of the colony while the people of {OTHER} think a little worse; side with {OTHER}, and it is the other way round. Or keep out of it, which pleases nobody much.

LanguageData.CC_Vassal_AskWhat_Camp: Given, the colony's word holds a season: the camp gone by then (a caravan of the colony's can attack it), their head thinks much better of the colony; still standing, worse. The colony can also say it can't.
LanguageData.CC_Vassal_Ask_Defend: {WHO} writes from {TOWN}: {OTHER} have come against them, and they ask the colony's fighters to stand with them.
LanguageData.CC_Vassal_AskWhat_Defend: Two of the colony's fighters or more should reach {TOWN} by caravan within five days and join the fight there through its own "Join fight". Their head will remember who came, and who didn't.
LanguageData.CC_Vassal_Ask_Release: {WHO} of {TOWN} writes that their people no longer wish to hold of the colony, and asks to be released.
LanguageData.CC_Vassal_AskWhat_Release: Released, they go on as their own town, without blame on either side. Refused, they break away: the tie broken, and their people think 15 worse of the colony.

LanguageData.CC_Vassal_AskWhat_Protection: Taken in, it brings produce at harvest as the council sets it, its levies can be called when a raid comes, and it will look to the colony in hard times, against camps near it and in quarrels with its neighbors.
